The write-set-size scoping this round introduced is NOT stated the same way everywhere it appears in requirements.md: one sibling statement of the same fact still asserts the superseded, unnarrowed rule. (1) Exact text: Roles and Permissions, requirements.md:976-988, names the running Resolver process 'the sole intended writer of live facet-manifest.yaml/capability-summary.yaml/project-context.resolved.json/Resolver Evidence instances for a real Feature, via the guarded journaled publication transaction REQ-001 fixes (staged generation, journaled transactional commit, cwd-independent path resolution per ADR-0025 ...)'. That governs Resolver Evidence unconditionally and names 'journaled transactional commit' as the mechanism. It contradicts REQ-001 step (m), requirements.md:336-341 ('That one-member write set is published directly, not through the journaled transaction ... a single temp file + fsync + rename onto resolver-evidence.yaml's own live path, with no staging area and no journal'), and REQ-004, requirements.md:594-599 ('When Evidence is the only thing this invocation writes -- every Block at REQ-001's (0)/(a)/(h)/(i)/(k)/(l)/(m) except (k)'s self-referential case -- REQ-001 step (m) fixes a single temp file + fsync + rename directly onto its live path, with no staging area and no journal'). Main Workflows 4 (requirements.md:1048-1059) and TEST-047 (acceptance-tests.md:93, 'written directly per REQ-001 step (m)') follow the narrowed rule; Roles and Permissions does not. (2) Downstream failure mode: the Phase-2 implementer of resolve-project-context, and the task author writing the publication-journal-recovery and disabled-legacy-invocation fixtures, cannot decide from requirements.md alone whether a sole-Evidence Block opens a journal -- which is verbatim the question attempt 6 round 2's Major raised ('the write mechanism for a sole-Evidence Block was specified twice, incompatibly', investigation.md:1502-1509). Resolved the Roles way, the (0) Block would open a second journal against the very Feature whose journal it just declared unconvergeable, which REQ-001 step (m) itself calls 'incoherent' (requirements.md:342-346), and the next invocation's mandatory recovery scan would then find that fresh journal instead of the unrecoverable one. (3) This belongs to spec review: both statements are inside this package's own frozen Phase-1 requirements.md, one in a Roles-and-Permissions writer/mechanism constraint and one in a goal's processing rule; no design, task, or quality-gate artifact is needed to see the conflict. (4) Severity Major, not Critical: REQ-001 step (m) and REQ-004 are specific, dated and carry the ruling-D(2) provenance, so the more specific text resolves the conflict for a careful reader and no acceptance row fails by construction -- but the remediation's own stated method was to locate every sibling statement of this fact before writing any of them (investigation.md:1517-1523), and this sibling inside the same document was missed, so the ambiguity round 2 identified persists in requirements.md. Supporting, not independently failing: no acceptance criterion locks the write-set-size rule outside TEST-047's single publication-journal-recovery fixture -- AC-011/AC-038 scope their guarantee to the three publication artifacts only, and AC-039/AC-054 test the journal from the failure and reader sides -- so nothing else in the acceptance surface would catch an implementation that followed the Roles wording.
